sourceNote: The cat mesh (assets/models/cat/README.md), with new arm faces: a cut along the arm seam, a side wall of the trunk under each arm, and a quad tube for each arm. The trunk is an even oval. tools/blender/cat_arms.py replays the Blender session that made it. cat.glb stays unchanged.
paintedNote: The weights of the arm tubes are the automatic weights of Blender with the Weight Paint fixes of tools/blender/cat_arms.py. The trunk, the side walls, the socket, and the first ring of each shoulder keep the rule weights, so that the chest in front of each shoulder does not fold.

armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone of this length in units, as on the rabbit. The app turns them from the joints of the pose (poseArm() of src/models/studio-rig.ts). They replace the rings of refine.

rootNormals.note: The skin faces whose middle lies within radius (units) of the head of an upper arm take the skin normals with no crease angle in the app (root_rim() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The bind turns the arm root, and without this rule hard dark lines show at the back of each arm root.

armSmooth.note: 4 rounds of taubin() smooth the tube of the bow arm of cat-arms.glb after the weights (arm_smooth() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that the arm shows no lumps. More rounds fold the bow paw.

name: Cat

app.note: The scale is 1.639161 m for each unit, so that the standing ear tips with the leg factor 1.5 are 1.758 m high, as the red fox. The trunk factor makes the cat shorter: the standing shoulder joints are at 1.042897 m (keptHeight() of tools/rig-mesh.ts). The reach is the reach of cat-arms.glb.

armFactorNote: The factor 1 does not stretch the arms in the rig. The upper arm of cat-arms.glb is 0.92 and the forearm 0.78 as long as on the source (step_shape() of tools/blender/cat_arms.py). The cat plays a smaller viola nearer to the neck, so that the left paw reaches the nut.
legFactorNote: The factor of the thigh and the shin. Each one stretches only between its joints, and the foot keeps its size. The factor is 1.5 + (1 - 0.85768) × 0.45 / 0.145 = 1.94168, so that the standing ear tips stay at 1.758 m with the shorter trunk.
neckFactorNote: The factor of the neck between its joints, the factor of the fox. The head keeps its size and moves down the neck with the head joint: the neck joint is 4.9 cm from the head joint.
girthFactorNote: The factors of the width and the depth of the trunk and the clavicles across the trunk axis (girth_moves() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that the trunk matches docs/reference/cat-views.png. The arms, the legs, and the tail keep their sizes and move out with their joints.
trunkFactorNote: The factor of the trunk between the hips joint and the neck joint (trunk_moves() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). From the narrowest neck row to the crotch, the trunk is 1.76 head heights, as on the red fox. The head, the arms, the legs, and the tail keep their sizes and move with the trunk.
jointsNote: The places are in the studio units and axes of the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the ear tips, +z forward, +x the left side. The tail is a chain of two bones. The elbow, the wrist, and the paw joints move with the shorter arm bones of cat-arms.glb.

studio.trunkNote: The trunk of the seated bind sits upright (trunk_turn() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py): the pelvis turns back until the hip angle opens by open degrees, and each trunk bone takes its share. With open 1, the trunk axis leans 0.4 degrees back, and no crease face turns over.
studio.bindArmsNote: The bind upper arm points 38 degrees from the hanging upper arm of the mesh, as on the deer. A bind farther from the mesh folds the socket at the back of the upper arm, and a bind nearer to it twists the arm more.
studio.bindSupinationNote: The bind paw of the left arm turns 120 degrees about its bind forearm toward supination (paw_supination() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The bind paw sets the zero of the paw twist, so the left paw does not twist through 180 degrees on the viola. The right paw keeps the bind arms.

tailCurl.note: The seated tail curls on the seat around the left side of the haunch, as a sitting cat curls its tail. The points are the curve after the tail root in the seated bind (curl_line() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The blend keeps the tail root with the haunch, and smooth rounds the curl.

studio.note: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind to the source: the thigh slopes 25 degrees down and 8 degrees out, and the shin is vertical (tools/rig/leg_turns.py <config> 25 8 0). The bind arms are the arms of the fox and the rabbit.

weights.armSplitNote: The side wall under each arm and the socket lie inside the plane |x| = 0.1, and below the armpit line at the height 0.6 they keep no arm weight (armBelow). A smaller value gives the side wall the weights of the free arm.
weights.stretchRampNote: With a ramp, the upper arm stretches by the arm factor only on the free arm: the share of the stretch fades from 0 to 1 over this many units on each side of the plane |x| = armSplit. 0 gives no ramp, as for the fox and the rabbit.

noseFront.note: The tips of the lower whiskers hang below headFrom, in front of the plane z = front, and only they lie there. The rule gives them to the head, so that the head lift does not bend each whisker. The head measures leave the tips out (headFloor of tools/studio-body.ts).

sliver.note: The corners of each thin face share one set of weights, so that the face moves rigidly and does not turn over at a bent joint. A thin face has a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge below longest (units), which takes face 1248 of the left armpit.

line.note: The middle corner of each long thin face (a corner angle above angle, in degrees) takes the mix of the weights of its two other corners by its place along their line, so that it does not lag when a joint bends. With head, the head takes the rule too.

weights.clavicleFromNote: The share of the clavicle weight that a vertex keeps grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height (units), and the chest takes the rest. This is the rule of the fox, moved with the clavicle joint of the cat (y 0.645).
weights.armTopNote: The share of the weight of the clavicles and the upper arms that a vertex keeps falls from 1 at the lower height to 0 at the upper height (units), and the neck takes the rest. Thus the bow arm does not fold the clavicle faces under the chin.
weights.shoulderRampNote: Above the heights of y (units), the share of the upper arm weight that a vertex keeps grows from 0 at the distance x[0] from the middle plane to 1 at x[1], and the clavicle takes the rest. Thus the top of the narrow shoulder next to the neck does not fold.
weights.shoulderHeadNote: Below headFrom, the share of the head weight that goes to the neck grows from 0 at the smaller distance from the middle plane to all at the larger distance (units). The values of the fox, scaled by the neck of the cat.
weights.fingersNote: The fingers keep this share of their bone heat weight, and the hand takes the rest, as in the fox and the rabbit.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the buttocks stay on the hips and the thigh turns onto the seat. The ramp of the fox, scaled by the thigh of the cat.

weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones. Above headFrom, each vertex except the ears follows the head only, with the whiskers. The vertices within radius of the tail line and behind the plane z = behind follow the two tail bones with soft shares.

refine.ringsNote: No ring: the quad tube of each arm has rings at the elbow and the wrist (tools/blender/cat_arms.py).

flip.note: The long edge of an arm face with a corner angle above angle (degrees) in the seated bind flips to the corner of the face on its other side, when the two faces lie almost on one plane (normals, degrees) and the surface moves at most move (units).

pointFlip.note: The edge at this point is the diagonal of one quad of the tube at the inner right elbow (point_flips() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The bow elbow bends far, and with this diagonal its thin face folds. With the other diagonal, it does not fold.

check.note: pnpm rig-mesh --check lists the faces of the seated bind with a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge of at least length (units), when that edge passes within near (units) of an arm or leg joint. These faces are candidates for a ring (refine.rings).

tone.note: The warm stage light adds chroma to the gray fur and the cream belly. Each plain fur face moves half of the full step to the sheet colors: a row is [L, dL, da, db] in Oklab. The paws, the whiskers, the pink nose, and the inner ears keep their colors.

belly.note: The light belly patch is an even oval in the front plane of the stretched trunk (belly_patch() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). Each face of the trunk front in the range takes the cream, the gray, or a mix by the share of its area in the oval.

colors.note: Each face takes the mean color of the texture at a grid of samples. A face is dark when at least eyeShare of its samples are below dark. The eye box and the nose box find the eye faces and the pink nose faces. Then palette and tone set the color.

eyeShell.note: Each eye shell is a fan from the middle of the dark eye faces to at most points points of their edge, lifted lift units. pnpm studio-body finds each eye by its fan, and the app puts its pea eye there (design 4.5). The values of the fox.

smooth.note: The rig smooths the neck and the bottom of the head inside the box before the weights, so that the underside of the big head shows no black band in its own shadow. The chin, the jaw, the muzzle, and the eyes stay outside the box.

chair.note: The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. The half width holds the haunch (x ±0.151). The front edge ends where the sloped thighs leave the seat top.

crease.note: The seated bind is smoothed across the crease where the belly meets the top of each thigh (crease_relax() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), with the values of the fox and the rabbit. The corrective shapes give the source back, so the standing body keeps its form.
crease.lapNote: A second smoothing (lap) of the seam between the oval belly and the thighs. It reaches 4 rings up the belly front and fades out over fade units behind the hip joints and beyond side units from the middle plane, so that the seat top and the outer hips stay.

sit.note: The underside of the haunch behind the hip joints goes down onto the seat in the seated bind (sit() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). With root, the tail root moves with the haunch. top keeps the seat top fixed, because the curled tail does not pull the root down.

bind.note: Each vertex with a weight on a lower bone of the left arm takes the dual quaternion blend in the seated bind (bind_skin() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that the elbow and the forearm keep the round tube. The bow arm bends further in the play, so it keeps the linear blend.

raise.note: The shape of the raised left arm of the play (pnpm raise-fit violist --faces 1594 --side L). In the pose of the rule, the skin near the points at the front of the arm root moves with the first upper arm segment (follow) and fills its valleys (fill).

The shape of the left arm at rest (pnpm raise-fit violist --faces 2255,2241,2242,2243 --side L --sets rest). In the pose of the rule, the same points as in the play shape move half of the way with the first upper arm segment.

The shape of the left arm between the rest and the play (pnpm raise-fit violist --faces 2488,2487,3118 --side L --sets lift). The upper arm passes between the turns of the other two shapes there, so this shape keeps the front of the root free of a crease in the lift.

The shape of the bow arm in the play (pnpm raise-fit violist --faces 772,775,689,690,729,688,691 --side R). In the pose of the rule, the vertices near 6 points at the front of the right root move half of the way with the first upper arm segment.
